rules.topic: ProjectExpansion replaces ProjectE's 3 collector/relay tiers with a 16-step matter ladder: BASIC, DARK, RED, MAGENTA, PINK, PURPLE, VIOLET, BLUE, CYAN, GREEN, LIME, YELLOW, ORANGE, WHITE, FADING, FINAL (level = position 1-16); DARK and RED coincide with ProjectE's dark/red matter

Collector generation scales by a factor of 6 per matter tier: output value = 4 x 6^(tier position), starting at 4 for BASIC (so DARK = 144, RED = 864, and FINAL = 4 x 6^15); the scaling function multiplies the base by 6 once per tier step (Matter.getValue)
Relay bonus and transfer scale by the same factor of 6 per tier: bonus = 1 x 6^(tier position), transfer = 64 x 6^(tier position) (relay transfer base at Matter.java line 51)
A FINAL-tier relay has effectively unlimited transfer (Long.MAX_VALUE); relay throughput stops being a bottleneck only at the final tier

ProjectExpansion star items (its Klein-star successors) have EMC capacities starting at 204800000 EMC and multiplying by 4 per step across an 18-entry table, dwarfing ProjectE's Klein Star Omega (51200000, see the projecte rule file)

rules.quote: public static final ForgeConfigSpec.ConfigValue<Integer> tickDelay = Builder.comment("The delay between mod operations (in ticks, default 20) - this will slightly effect the amount of emc generated via rounding - increase if you're noticing lag").defineInRange("tickDelay", 20, 1, 200);
rules.topic: Mod operations (including collector processing) run on a configurable cadence of 20 ticks by default (config tickDelay, 1-200); generation figures are realized in steps at this cadence

rules.quote: public static final ForgeConfigSpec.ConfigValue<Double> collectorMultiplier = Builder.comment("Multiplies the output of Collectors.").defineInRange("collectorMultiplier", 1.0D, 0.1D, 50D);
rules.topic: Collector output has a global config multiplier (default 1.0, range 0.1-50); quoted generation assumes the default

rules.quote: public static final ForgeConfigSpec.ConfigValue<Integer> transmutationInterfaceItemCount = Builder.comment("The amount of items that the transmutation interface will report to have. Depending on your usage, you may want this to be a high value.").defineInRange("transmutationInterfaceItemCount", Integer.MAX_VALUE, 1, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
rules.topic: The transmutation interface exposes the owner's learned items to automation (e.g. AE2) and reports a stock count of Integer.MAX_VALUE per item by default: external systems see learned items as effectively infinite, with the EMC pool as the real constraint
